proposals.target: checklist Apple table, new row Content safety (C07)
proposals.text: Content safety: test app content, UGC, AI output and metadata against 1.1 and 1.4 (defamation or discrimination, realistic violence, weapons, sexual or hookup content, religious commentary, fake or prank features, exploiting current events, drugs, alcohol and tobacco, DUI checkpoints and risky challenges) independently of the age rating answers.

proposals.target: checklist Baseline Reviewer access row (C03)
proposals.text: Apple review notes and App Review information state the business model, every new or changed feature with navigation steps, non-obvious features and IAP, devices tested, external services, regional differences, a required-hardware video, an expired-subscription demo account, regulatory or rights documents and a current App Review contact.

proposals.target: checklist Baseline Listing row (C04)
proposals.text: Apple listing extras: items needing extra purchase are marked, promoted IAP name, image and description, in-app events and creative assets meet metadata rules, a pre-order listing matches the release, and neither the build nor the listing is a beta, demo or trial version.

proposals.target: checklist Apple table, new row Runtime conduct (C03, C19)
proposals.text: Runtime conduct: no forced ratings, reviews or downloads and only the system review prompt, push not required and marketing push opt-in with in-app opt-out and no sensitive data, no suggested restarts or unrelated settings changes, no altered system controls or alternate home screens, a visible indicator while recording, and no excessive battery, heat or unrelated background work such as mining.

proposals.target: checklist Apple Submission row (C09)
proposals.text: Binary checks: private API use, deprecated frameworks, downloaded or interpreted code that changes features, native APIs exposed to mini apps or plug-ins, a non-WebKit browser engine without entitlement, IPv6-only network operation, hidden, dormant or obfuscated features, and scraping of Apple sites.

proposals.target: checklist Apple table, new row Platform technologies (C09)
proposals.text: Platform technologies: from entitlements, extensions and linked frameworks, check each used technology against its clause, including App Clips, widgets and notifications, app, keyboard and Safari extensions, SiriKit, CallKit and SMS filters, face authentication, file pickers, Matter, MusicKit, Game Center, Apple Pay, Wallet passes, embedded Apple emoji, tvOS controllers and Mac App Store rules.

proposals.target: special-cases new section Regulated services (C20)
proposals.text: For Apple regulated categories, record the submitting entity, licence and territory evidence for medical claims (including a consult-a-doctor reminder), drug dosage calculators, criminal-activity reporting, crypto wallets, mining, exchanges and ICOs, insurance, nonprofit fundraising and charity collection, trading, CFDs and binary options, personal loans with APR and term disclosure, and MDM.

proposals.target: special-cases AI, health, kids and UGC (C16)
proposals.text: Creator content, mini apps, mini games, streaming games, chatbots, plug-ins and emulators: inventory all non-embedded software, apply moderation, privacy and payment rules to it, require per-instance consent before sharing data or permissions, verify an index with universal links, and verify that content above the age rating is labelled and restricted by verified or declared age.

proposals.target: special-cases Expo / React Native / RevenueCat / AdMob, ads paragraph (C13)
proposals.text: For Apple ads, verify no ads in extensions, App Clips, widgets, notifications, keyboards or watchOS apps, an in-app view of targeting information, no targeting from health, ClassKit or kids data, clearly marked interstitials with visible close buttons, an in-app report-ad option and no inflated impressions or ad-dominant design.

proposals.target: special-cases Games, coins and gambling (C14)
proposals.text: For Apple sweepstakes, contests and raffles, verify the developer is the sponsor and that official rules shown in the app state Apple is not a sponsor or involved.

proposals.target: checklist Apple Purchases row (C11)
proposals.text: Confirm no paid item or subscription monetizes built-in hardware, OS capabilities or Apple services such as push notifications, the camera, iCloud storage or Screen Time.

requirements.text: Request permissions incrementally in context and get new affirmative consent before using data for new purposes

items.title: Google Play's Target API Level Policy

requirements.text: New apps and app updates target an API level within one year of the latest major Android release
requirements.note: Google Build/release row names target API.

requirements.text: Existing apps not updated must target within two years of the latest major release to stay available to new users on newer Android versions
requirements.note: Audit inspects the submitted build; visibility of the live, not-updated version is not named.

requirements.text: Target API extensions requested through Play Console
requirements.note: Optional console process, not a build requirement.

requirements.text: No interference with or unauthorized access to the device, other apps, networks, APIs, Google services or carrier networks
requirements.note: General prohibition; only specific behaviours below are checkable.

requirements.text: Comply with default Android system optimization requirements in the Core App Quality guidelines
requirements.note: Runtime quality is tested, but Core App Quality system optimization is not referenced.

requirements.text: App does not modify, replace or update itself by any method other than Google Play's update mechanism
requirements.note: No control checks self-update or in-app APK update code.

requirements.text: App and SDKs do not download executable code (dex, JAR, .so) from outside Google Play; runtime-loaded interpreted code (for example OTA JavaScript) must not enable policy violations
requirements.note: Expo/React Native OTA updates are not reviewed against this rule anywhere.

requirements.text: No code that introduces or exploits security vulnerabilities; address App Security Improvement Program alerts
requirements.note: Pending console tasks may show ASI alerts, but security vulnerability review is not named.

requirements.text: No WebView with an added JavaScript interface loading untrusted (http) or unverified URLs
requirements.note: No WebView configuration check exists.

requirements.text: Do not bypass system power management unless eligible for allowlisting
requirements.note: Background behaviour is in C19 scope but battery optimization exemptions are not named.

requirements.text: Proxy services to third parties only when that is the app's primary user-facing purpose (includes SDKs)
requirements.note: SDK inventory lists SDKs but proxyware behaviour is not named.

requirements.text: No game cheating, hacking facilitation, ad blocking of other apps, or use of a service/API in violation of its terms
requirements.note: C08 covers rights and originality, not ToS-violating API use or cheat/hacking functionality.

requirements.text: Full-screen intent not used to force interaction with disruptive ads or notifications
No circumvention of Android sandbox protections to derive user activity or identity from other apps
requirements.note: Only indirectly reached through permission review.

requirements.text: Foreground services: beneficial core feature, user-initiated or perceptible, user-stoppable, not deferrable, runs only as long as needed; valid types and declaration for API 34+
requirements.note: FGS named in Permissions row.

requirements.text: User-initiated data transfer jobs used only for user-initiated network transfers and only as long as needed
requirements.note: UIDT jobs not named.

requirements.text: Respect other apps' FLAG_SECURE; no workarounds; accessibility tools must not transmit or cache protected content
requirements.note: Applies to screen capture, recording, casting and accessibility apps; no check exists and no feature gate makes it N/A.

requirements.text: On-device Android container apps honour REQUIRE_SECURE_ENV and do not proxy APIs or load older versions to bypass it
requirements.note: Niche: only Android container apps; no check exists.

items.title: Understanding Google Play's app account deletion requirements

requirements.text: Complete the Data deletion questions in the Data safety form
requirements.note: Console evidence for Data safety and deletion URL.

requirements.text: Apps enabling account creation provide an in-app path to delete account and associated data
Account creation counts even when the app sends users to an external creation flow, or when only part of the app needs an account
requirements.note: Accounts feature gate wording does not say externally created accounts trigger the requirement.

requirements.text: In-app path may be a link to the web deletion resource; path must be prominent, for example in account settings
requirements.note: Runtime check of the in-app path.

requirements.text: Web resource provides a deletion request route without requiring reinstalling or returning to the app
requirements.note: G03 checks the URL exists and works; not that it works without the app.

requirements.text: Web link functional, deletion pathway prominent, and references app or developer name exactly as on the store listing
requirements.note: Naming match and prominence not stated.

requirements.text: Prerequisite steps (for example cancelling a subscription) clearly outlined with a support flow; if reusing a privacy page, deletion section highlighted (anchor link)
requirements.note: Not stated in checklist.

requirements.text: Delete user data in scope (all data declared collected in Data safety) and request service providers to delete shared data
requirements.note: Associated-data removal is checked on own systems; requesting deletion by processors is not named.

requirements.text: Inform users what to expect and fulfil requests within a reasonably quick period
requirements.note: Timeframe disclosure not checked.

requirements.text: Disclose retention for security, fraud or regulatory reasons
Exemptions: permanently private and enterprise apps; offline-only accounts are not app accounts
requirements.note: Applicability is decided through the accounts gate with N/A justification.

requirements.text: Non-mobile surfaces (TV, Wear OS) may omit in-app path but still need the web resource and Console URL
requirements.note: G03 requires the external resource regardless.

requirements.text: Deadline history: Data deletion questions required from December 7, 2023, extension to May 31, 2024
requirements.note: Past deadlines, now enforced; no future date.

requirements.text: Developer is responsible for SDK code and practices; know SDK permissions, data collected and why
requirements.note: Special-cases: native dependencies can add permissions; C06 SDK inventory.

requirements.text: SDK data collection aligns with app's disclosed purposes; no SDK sale of personal data
requirements.note: Sale and secondary use by SDKs (for example anti-fraud SDK sharing for ads) are not named.

requirements.text: SDK data handled securely (HTTPS) and runtime permissions requested before access
Default-collecting SDKs must meet prominent disclosure and consent
requirements.note: Same gap as User Data prominent disclosure.

requirements.text: SDKs must not link persistent device IDs (IMEI) to location or AAID to persistent IDs or email
requirements.note: Linkage named generically only.

requirements.text: SDK transmission of installed packages needs disclosure and privacy policy coverage
requirements.note: Package inventory is sensitive but not called out.

requirements.text: Child-directed apps include only Families self-certified SDKs
Data safety includes data collected by third-party libraries and SDKs
SDK permissions only for current features promoted in the listing; not for undisclosed purposes (for example background location)
requirements.note: Permissions row: merged manifest vs core purpose.

requirements.text: No malware or spyware via SDKs: no credential theft, privilege escalation, SELinux disabling, uninstall prevention, billing fraud, covert data exfiltration
requirements.note: No control inspects SDKs for malicious or spyware behaviour; checkable via dependency and traffic review.

requirements.text: No SDK downloading executable code (dex/native) from outside Play, self-updating APKs, or installing apps from unknown sources
requirements.note: No code-integrity check exists.

requirements.text: No webview JavaScript interface loading untrusted (http or unverified) URLs; no insecure file downloads
requirements.note: No security review of webviews or transport for downloads.

requirements.text: SDK proxy services only when proxy is the app's core user-facing purpose
requirements.note: Not inspected.

requirements.text: SDK foreground services need an appropriate use case and must be declared in the manifest
requirements.note: Checklist Permissions row names FGS.

requirements.text: No SDK review-evasion techniques or hidden, dormant features
requirements.note: Nothing directs the auditor to look for review evasion or hidden features.

requirements.text: Accurate description, images and video of functionality in metadata

Ads SDK and mediation provider obligations: ad content definitions, creative rating, watermarking, ad formats, child-directed treatment, no IBA, RTB indicators, identifier restrictions, test app, documentation
requirements.note: Obligations on SDK providers enrolling in the program, not on the app under audit.

requirements.text: App using mediation to serve children must only mediate Families self-certified SDKs or equivalent safeguards and pass content rating and child-directed signals
requirements.note: SDK eligibility is checked but mediation adapters and child-directed signal propagation are not named.

requirements.text: Families ad format rules (closeable after 5 seconds, single placement, clearly distinguishable, no deceptive dismiss)
requirements.note: See Families policy item; not stated in skill.

requirements.text: Apps whose target audience is only children and that serve ads use only self-certified ads SDK versions
requirements.note: C15 SDK eligibility; special-cases ads inspects SDK versions and age settings.

requirements.text: Mixed-audience apps ensure ads to children come only from self-certified SDK versions, for example via neutral age screen
requirements.note: Special-cases Kids: actual age flows and SDK/ad eligibility.

requirements.text: In-house cross-promotion and direct deals are exempt from self-certification but still subject to User Data and Families policy
requirements.note: Applicability nuance.

requirements.text: SDK-side self-certification requirements (registration in SDK Console, ratings method, documentation)
requirements.note: Applies to SDK providers.

requirements.text: Declare target audience age groups accurately in Target audience and content before publishing; only select groups the app is designed for
Imagery and terminology appealing to children can change Google's assessment of declared audience
requirements.note: Checklist Audience row compares actual content to intended ages.

requirements.text: Accurate Play Console answers incl. Target audience, Data safety and IARC questionnaire, updated with changes
Content accessible to children is appropriate for children
App must not be merely a webview or primarily drive affiliate traffic without permission
requirements.note: Substantive functionality.

requirements.text: Disclose collection of sensitive info from children incl. via APIs and SDKs
Child-only apps must not transmit AAID, SIM serial, build serial, BSSID, MAC, SSID, IMEI, IMSI; mixed apps not from children or unknown-age users
requirements.note: Identifier transmission by kids apps is not named.

requirements.note: Not named.

requirements.note: Not named for kids.

requirements.note: Not named.

requirements.note: Special-cases Kids: SDK/ad eligibility and age flows.

requirements.text: AR sections show a safety warning on launch (parental supervision, physical hazards); no devices advised against for children
requirements.note: Not named.

Social apps and features for children: in-app online-safety reminder before exchanging freeform media, adult action before exchanging personal info, adult controls over social features
requirements.note: Specific reminder and adult-action mechanics are not named.

requirements.text: Anonymous or stranger chat apps must not target children
requirements.note: Audience row lists chat.

requirements.text: Comply with COPPA, GDPR and other child laws including via SDKs
requirements.note: Legal determination.

requirements.text: Ads to children or unknown-age users: only self-certified SDKs, no interest-based ads or remarketing, child-appropriate ad content
requirements.note: Special-cases ads: age settings and consent; Kids: SDK/ad eligibility.

requirements.text: Distinguish virtual game coins from real money for in-app purchases in kids apps; no overly aggressive commercial tactics
requirements.note: Not named.

requirements.note: Actual content review.

requirements.note: Audience row compares content to intended ages.

requirements.note: C16 reporting; G01 Child safety standards declaration.

requirements.note: Self-certification of operational process; declaration presence falls under G01.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, new Code integrity row (C09, C19)
proposals.text: Code integrity: confirm the build does not self-update or download executable code or behaviour-changing JavaScript outside Play, load untrusted URLs into WebViews with a JavaScript interface, hide or remotely enable features after review, block uninstall, prompt users to disable Play Protect, bundle undisclosed software, include SDKs that proxy traffic, exfiltrate data or evade review, or interfere with other apps, devices, servers or networks.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, Permissions row (C19)
proposals.text: Also check each restricted permission or API actually used against its policy: SMS and Call Log default-handler rule, MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES (no self-update, no embedded installers), USE_EXACT_ALARM, battery optimization exemption, user-initiated data transfer jobs, Age Signals API purpose, photo and video pickers for minimum scope, no sale of permission-derived data, a working video link per foreground service type, and Accessibility API or VpnService use disclosed in the listing with in-app prominent disclosure, consent, isAccessibilityTool where applicable and encrypted VPN traffic.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, Permissions row (C19), upcoming requirements
proposals.text: Before each audit compare the build against announced permission deadlines: location button and ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION declaration for API 37+ and Contact Picker for non-broad contacts access (2027-01-27), READ_CALL_LOG phone-call verification and geofencing foreground service removal (2027-01-27), AppFunctions rules (2027-04-14), Local Network declaration for API 37+ and MANAGE_CONTACTS declaration (2027-08-25).

proposals.target: special-cases, new section Monitoring, screen capture and containers (C19)
proposals.text: Monitoring or tracking apps must set the isMonitoringTool flag, show a persistent notification and unique icon and disclose monitoring in the Play description, and screen capture or container apps must honour FLAG_SECURE and REQUIRE_SECURE_ENV.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, Data safety row (G02, C06)
proposals.text: Also verify a prominent in-app disclosure appears in normal use immediately before each runtime permission or personal and sensitive data collection, names the data and its use, and obtains affirmative consent not inferred from dismissal, and that identifiers follow Play rules: no linking of persistent hardware IDs, AAID only for ads or analytics with opt-out respected and never linked to persistent IDs, App Set ID not used for ads, no sale of personal data by the app or its SDKs, and no public exposure of financial, payment, government ID or non-public contact data.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, Privacy row (C05)
proposals.text: Privacy policy URL is labeled as a privacy policy, active, public, served over valid SSL, not geofenced or behind login, a standard non-editable webpage rather than a PDF or download, linked in Play Console and inside the app, and discloses location use for ads with links to ad network privacy policies where applicable.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, Deletion row (G03)
proposals.text: The external deletion resource names the app or developer exactly as on the listing, shows a prominent request path usable without reinstalling the app, outlines prerequisite steps such as cancelling subscriptions, lists retained data and retention periods, and applies also when accounts can be created outside the app.

proposals.target: special-cases, AI, health, kids and UGC, Kids line (C15)
proposals.text: For Google Families apps also check that no AAID, hardware ID, phone number or (in child-only apps) location is collected from children, the AD_ID permission is absent in child-only apps targeting API 33+, Bluetooth uses Companion Device Manager, AR features show a safety warning, social features have safety reminders and adult action, and ads meet Families format limits (closable after 5 seconds, no launch interstitial, distinguishable from content) from self-certified SDKs only.

proposals.target: special-cases, Expo / React Native / RevenueCat / AdMob, ads sentence (C13)
proposals.text: For Google also check that ads stay within the app content rating, do not imitate system UI or notifications, do not appear outside the app, over other apps or on the lockscreen, follow Better Ads timing (no interstitial before splash or at level start, closable within 15 seconds, no consecutive made-for-ads interstitials), and show no ad fraud signals such as hidden ads, automatic clicks, fake install attribution or misreported package or platform.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, App content row (G01)
proposals.text: Real-money gambling, dating, random stranger chat and anonymous chat apps have Play Console tools for blocking minors configured, and social, dating and chat apps have a publicly posted child safety standards page explicitly prohibiting CSAE plus the child safety contact declaration.

proposals.target: special-cases, AI, health, kids and UGC, UGC/chat line (C16)
proposals.text: For Google also check that users accept terms defining objectionable content before posting, incidental sexual content is filtered by default behind an age screen, UGC monetization has safeguards, AR content anchoring is moderated, and anonymous or random chat, social and dating apps meet child safety standards, age restrictions and do not target children.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, Billing row (C11)
proposals.text: Also check anti-steering in listing, webviews and sign-up flows, cases that must not use Play billing (physical goods, clinical services, real-money gambling), loot box odds disclosure before purchase, and digital purchases offered through AI or agentic experiences.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, Subscription UI row (C12)
proposals.text: Also check that terms are visible without extra user action, SKU names are accurate with no Free Trial naming for auto-renewing products, flows cannot cause accidental subscription, recurring value is not reduced after purchase, and from 2027-01-27 eligibility-based discounts disclose eligibility criteria, verification process and post-eligibility price and benefits.

proposals.target: special-cases, new section Financial services and crypto (C20)
proposals.text: Loan and earned-wage-access apps use the Finance category, state APR, repayment period and total cost in metadata, respect the 60-day minimum and US 36% APR limits and the prohibited sensitive-permission list, binary options are absent, and crypto apps do no on-device mining, flag tokenized digital assets in in-app products and do not glamorize earnings.

proposals.target: special-cases, Games, coins and gambling (C14)
proposals.text: For Google real-money gambling also confirm the app is free to download, does not use Play billing for wagers, shows responsible gambling information in app and listing, and that gamified loyalty programs follow their separate rules.

proposals.target: special-cases, AI, health, kids and UGC, Health line (C18)
proposals.text: For Google health apps also check the description disclaimer that the app is not a medical device with a consult-a-professional reminder, external hardware compatibility disclosure, research consent and ethics approval where applicable, Health Connect limited use and privacy policy content, and the Android 16 migration from BODY_SENSORS to android.permission.health permissions.

proposals.target: special-cases, AI, health, kids and UGC, AI line (C17)
proposals.text: Apps exposing AppFunctions must not deceive or manipulate AI agents, bypass security controls or interfere with other apps (Google, effective 2027-04-14).

proposals.target: checklist Baseline table, new Restricted content row (C07, C08)
proposals.text: Screen app content and listing for prohibited or restricted material: sexual content and explicit keywords, hate, violence and self-harm, extremism, sensitive events, bullying, weapons, drugs, tobacco and alcohol sales without age gating, fake ID or document generators, illegal activity facilitation and PII of non-consenting people.

proposals.target: checklist Baseline table, Quality row (C03)
proposals.text: Also check that the app does not change device settings without consent and reversibility, does not imitate OS alerts or misstate device state in notifications, does not incentivize or force ratings or reviews, sends messages on the user's behalf only after the user confirms content and recipients, prompts before large asset downloads, and behaves the same during review as for users.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, new Listing row (C04)
proposals.text: Google listing rules: title at most 30 characters, no emojis, special characters or non-brand all caps in title, icon or developer name, no ranking, price, promotion or Play program claims, no unattributed testimonials or keyword stuffing, all-ages listing images, correct category, no Official or affiliation claims or imitation of another app, Android brand use per the Android Brand Guidelines, and release notes non-promotional within 500 characters per language.

proposals.target: checklist Baseline table, Rights/originality row (C08)
proposals.text: Also check for features that induce IP infringement and for sale or promotion of counterfeit goods.

proposals.target: checklist Conditional modules, add News and magazines (G01)
proposals.text: News apps declared in App content identify article sources and authors, publish regular updates, show publisher contact information and third-party source details, and preview content before any subscription.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, Build/release row (C09)
proposals.text: Also check the two-year target API rule for availability to new users, latest Unicode emoji support for custom emoji libraries on Android 12+, the memory and code optimization quality thresholds announced for February 2027, and the updated Android XR quality guidelines for XR builds.

proposals.target: checklist Google table, Production access row (G04, C02)
proposals.text: Also check package name registration for Android developer verification, Organization account requirement for financial, health research, VPN and government apps with consistent D-U-N-S data, trader status declaration, Japan payments authorization due 2026-12-01, and that the production access application states tester feedback, changes made and readiness.

proposals.target: special-cases, Rejection response
proposals.text: For Google, recheck the whole app after a rejection because a violation notice may not list every issue.
